chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amriki Al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the man who prays upon the wet growing grass. He said: 'When he presses his forehead to the ground, there is no problem.' And (I asked him) about the thick growing lawn grass, which touches new ground. He said: 'No problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on wet grass?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the permissibility of praying on wet, growing grass by establishing a tactile criterion: if the vegetation is thick enough that the forehead presses through to touch the earth, the prayer is valid. This ruling distinguishes between mere surface coverage and substantial obstruction, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that natural, pure elements are permissible for sajdah unless they prevent direct contact with the ground.
